content:
# S3 Logs Buckets with ACK

Given that the repository uses bare Kubernetes manifests with ACK, I'll provide the bucket resources and IAM permission updates for both environments. Since I don't have the existing `iam.yaml` content, I'll show both options: (1) new separate policy files, and (2) how the existing User/Role would be updated.

## Dev Environment

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-dev
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/iam.yaml` (updated)
```yaml
---
# Existing User (shown with new logs policy added)
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: User
metadata:
  name: myapp-user
spec:
  userName: myapp-user
  inlinePolicies:
  - name: myapp-assets-policy
    policyDocument: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:ListBucket"],
            "Resource": [
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-dev",
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-dev/*"
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
  - name: myapp-logs-policy
    policyDocument: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
          }
        ]
      }
```

---

## Prod Environment

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-prod
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/iam.yaml` (updated)
```yaml
---
# Existing Role (shown with new logs policy added)
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-role
spec:
  roleName: myapp-role
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Principal": {
            "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B716D3041E"
          },
          "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
          "Condition": {
            "StringEquals": {
              "oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B716D3041E:sub": "system:serviceaccount:default:myapp"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  inlinePolicies:
  - name: myapp-assets-policy
    policyDocument: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:ListBucket"],
            "Resource": [
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-prod",
              "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-prod/*"
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
  - name: myapp-logs-policy
    policyDocument: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
          }
        ]
      }
```

---

### Summary

- **Buckets**: Each environment gets `myapp-logs-{env}` with versioning, AES-256 encryption, and full public access block.
- **Permissions**: New inline policies grant the existing User (dev) and Role (prod) `s3:GetObject` and `s3:PutObject` on logs buckets only — the existing policies for assets buckets remain unchanged.
- **Isolation**: Each `dev/` and `prod/` directory is fully self-contained; applying `dev/` changes only dev state.
